newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee plummets after Brazil escapes frost.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee plummets after Brazil escapes frost.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures tumbles in volatile trading on Tuesday morning, on commercial and local selling after top-grower Brazil escaped damaging frost overnight, dealers said.
July arabicas plunged to session low of 22556.00 cents before buyers emerged to pare losses. At 1013 EDT, July was down 17.30 cents, to 236.00 cents, after reaching a high of 259.70 at the opening.
Second-month September was 15.60 lower, at 210.00, while the back months fell 0.05 to 9.00.
On Monday, news that Brazilian forecasters were anticipating another cold night fueled a fund-led buying.

But cooperative officials in Brazil said this morning the coffee belt appeared to have seen the worst of a passing polar air mass, confirming a slightly milder night and no reports of any frosts on coffee farms.
"It was up 16 cents on the cold weather and there was no cold weather," one dealer said.
Weather Services Corp. said on Tuesday that temperatures would be cool this morning in Brazil's coffee belt, but no damaging cold was expected.

Brazil's weather is expected to turn milder over the next couple of days, with low temperatures on Wednesday in the 40s to lower 50s Fharenheit (F). Thursday's lows will range from 45 to 55 F, WSC said.
The downslide was accelerated after the July contract slid through key technical support at 239-238 cents basis July, traders said.
